title: Duolingo English Test: Format & Why It's Booming
summary: The ~1-hour, at-home, adaptive DET — how it's structured, the 10–160 score, and why 5,500+ universities now accept it.

chunks.heading: One hour, at home, adaptive
chunks.body: The Duolingo English Test (DET) takes about **an hour on your own computer** with a webcam — no test centre. The main **graded section is adaptive**: questions get harder or easier based on your answers, and there's **no fixed number of questions** — it ends when the scoring engine is confident of your level.
chunks.realExample: Because it's adaptive, two test-takers can see different questions and a different number of them. Do well early and you'll get harder items that let you reach a higher score.
chunks.memoryHook: No fixed length — it stops when it's sure of your level. Early answers set the ceiling.

chunks.heading: Mixed tasks, plus samples sent to universities
chunks.body: Rather than four separate sections, the DET **mixes short task types across reading, listening, speaking and writing**. Near the end you record a longer **Writing Sample** and **Speaking Sample (video)** that are **shared with the institutions** you send scores to, alongside your number.
chunks.realExample: So an admissions officer sees both your score AND a short video and writing sample — meaning your real communication, not just the number, is on show. Treat those samples seriously.
chunks.memoryHook: Score + a video + a writing sample all go to the university. The samples count too.

chunks.heading: Scored 10–160
chunks.body: The DET reports an **overall score from 10 to 160 in 5-point steps**, which is the **average of four skill subscores** (Reading, Writing, Speaking, Listening), rounded to the nearest 5. It also gives integrated subscores (see the scoring note).
chunks.realExample: A university asking for 'DET 120' wants an overall 120 — but many also set minimum subscores, so a strong overall with one weak skill can still fall short.
chunks.memoryHook: 10–160 overall = average of the 4 skills. Check subscore minimums too.

chunks.heading: Why it's exploding — and its one limit
chunks.body: The DET is **cheaper (~$65 vs $200+), faster (results in ~48 hours) and taken at home**, and it's now accepted by **5,500+ universities**, especially in the US. Its main limit: it is **not on the approved list for some visa/immigration routes** (e.g. UK visas), so confirm your destination accepts it.
chunks.realExample: For US university admission the DET is often ideal; for a UK Student visa you'll usually still need IELTS UKVI. Always check both the university AND the visa route.
chunks.memoryHook: Great for US admissions, cheap and fast — but check visa acceptance separately.

recall.q: How long is the Duolingo English Test and where is it taken?
recall.a: About one hour, at home on your own computer with a webcam — no test centre.

recall.q: Why does the number of questions vary between test-takers?
recall.a: The graded section is adaptive and has no fixed length — it ends when the scoring engine is confident of your level.

recall.q: What is the DET score range and how is the overall calculated?
recall.a: 10–160 in 5-point steps; the overall is the average of the four skill subscores (Reading, Writing, Speaking, Listening), rounded to the nearest 5.

recall.q: What extra material do universities receive besides your score?
recall.a: A Writing Sample and a Speaking Sample (video) recorded during the test are shared with the institutions you send scores to.

recall.q: What is the main limitation of the DET?
recall.a: It isn't accepted for every visa/immigration route (e.g. UK visas), so you must confirm your destination and visa accept it.
